explanation.text: For faba bean targeting cooked chicken flavor, the key missing meat-like notes are 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol (meaty/roasted) [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.1.0], sulfur-containing furan derivatives [1-s2.0-S0924224421002764-main.pdf p.11.0], Maillard reaction products including pyrazines [foods-12-00923.pdf p.4.0], and free glutamic acid for umami character [1-s2.0-S0924224421002764-main.pdf p.11.0]. Faba bean's dominant off-notes are hexanal (green, beany, grassy) [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.14.0], 2-isobutyl-3-methoxypyrazine (green) [s11947-025-03898-3.pdf p.3.0], vicine and convicine with phenolic acids (bitter) [s11947-025-03898-3.pdf p.3.0], and condensed tannins (astringent) [1-s2.0-S0268005X23012389-main.pdf p.1.0]. The top-ranked lever is a D-xylose and L-cysteine Maillard reaction system, which generates 2-methyl-3-furanthiol and 2-furfurylthiol directly [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.1.0] [1-s2.0-S0963996926007192-main.pdf p.2.0]. Lactic acid bacteria fermentation can reduce hexanal and methoxypyrazines [foods-15-00039.pdf p.9.0], while beta-cyclodextrin addresses residual beany aldehydes [journal.pone.0269278.pdf p.8.0]. Bitterness and astringency from faba-specific compounds may be reduced upstream via dehulling or low-tannin cultivar selection [s11947-025-03898-3.pdf p.9.0] [s11947-025-03898-3.pdf p.18.0].
